text.content:
Hard. A walled town that remembers last year.

Lantern Night: Bells rung every hour to keep the real monsters away. They never work.

The shopping list (5 items):

  1. A new lock for the dungeon (essential)
  2. The silver spoons (essential)
  3. Black-edged writing paper
  4. Bandages, lots
  5. A side of bacon

The furniture: a suit of armour (Bulky: one carrier), at the tailor (4).

Villagers: old Granny Mott, who has seen it all before (practising the bells); a gang of children (gossiping, loudly).

Hard: Suspicion Limit 15 · Difficulty: the way out 10, the lock-up 10 · the final flight: mob 11, Lead 2, escape at 6.

In Foundry

On the Raid HUD, New raid → Hard sets these numbers. To put this town’s list on the HUD (so its items show there and the end of the raid starts from them), run this as a script macro:

// Gallowsmere: put this shopping list on the Raid HUD (run as the Storyteller, after New raid → Hard).
game.dontGetForked.runOp("raid.list", { action: "set", list: [
  { name: "a new lock for the dungeon", duty: "handyman", essential: true },
  { name: "the silver spoons", duty: "butler", essential: true },
  { name: "black-edged writing paper", duty: "librarian", essential: false },
  { name: "bandages, lots", duty: "tailor", essential: false },
  { name: "a side of bacon", duty: "cook", essential: false }
] });

Each location’s rows run in order: its two ways in (picked the first time anyone tries the location, then kept for the raid), then each “Then”. The furniture’s obstacle is already 2 harder. It comes last, marked “for the piece”. Watched: Trouble there gets you caught. (group): each Entity rolls for itself. The loud way works too, at Suspicion +1 whatever the result. The kind in brackets is what one Castle Duty shops for. Any move takes one Turn (two carrying furniture).

Location · obstacleQuiet wayLoud wayDifficulty
1. The smithy: a new lock for the dungeon (tools and hardware) · essential
Way in A bolted back gate watchedBrawn (lift it off its hinges)Charm (shout “Delivery!” until someone opens it)10
or A high garden wall watchedNimbleBrawn (through the gate, lock and all)8
Then The night watchman on his round watchedWits (time his round)—10
2. The silversmith: the silver spoons (silver, china and linen) · essential
Way in A locked front door watchedSly (pick the lock)Brawn (kick it in)10
or A shuttered window watchedNimbleBrawn (force the shutters)8
Then A guard dog watchedCharm (a biscuit and a pat)Nimble (outrun it, barking)8
Then A locked strongboxWits (work out the catch)Charm (sweet-talk the clerk into opening it)10
3. The printer: black-edged writing paper (books and paper)
Way in A nosy neighbour at her window watchedSlyWits (a false alarm: “Your cat’s on the roof!”)8
or The rooftops (group)Nimble—10
Then A dark, cluttered back roomWitsSly (rummage through everything)8
4. The tailor: bandages, lots (cloth and costumes)
Way in A doorman checking invitations watchedCharmWits (a forged invitation that fools nobody for long)10
or A rickety drainpipeNimble—8
Then A crowded shop floor (group) watchedSly—10
Then A heavy cellar trapdoor for the pieceBrawn—12
5. The butcher: a side of bacon (food and drink)
Way in A muddy yard full of geese watchedSlyNimble (run for it, honking)8
or A cart blocking the alley watchedBrawnNimble (scramble over the load)10
Then The shopkeeper behind the counter watchedCharmSly (snatch it from under her nose)10
Then A tug-of-war across the lane (group)Brawn—12
